examples.src: We should set realistic goals for ourselves.
examples.dst: 我们应该为自己设定切合实际的目标。

examples.src: The painting is so realistic that it looks like a photo.
examples.dst: 这幅画非常逼真，看起来像一张照片。

examples.src: It is not realistic to finish the project in two days.
examples.dst: 想在两天内完成这个项目是不现实的。

confuse.diff: real 指真实的；realistic 指现实的、逼真的。

examples.src: Love is an abstract idea that is hard to define.
examples.dst: 爱是一个很难定义的抽象概念。

examples.src: She likes abstract paintings with bright colours.
examples.dst: 她喜欢色彩鲜艳的抽象画。

examples.src: Please read the abstract before the whole paper.
examples.dst: 请在读全文之前先读摘要。

confuse.diff: abstract 指抽象的；absorb 指吸收。

examples.src: There is a stone sculpture in front of the museum.
examples.dst: 博物馆前面有一座石雕。

examples.src: He studied sculpture at an art college.
examples.dst: 他在艺术学院学习雕塑。

examples.src: The sculpture was made of bronze.
examples.dst: 这件雕塑是用青铜制成的。

confuse.diff: sculpture 指雕塑作品；sculptor 指雕塑家。

examples.src: The sculptor spent two years making the statue.
examples.dst: 这位雕塑家花了两年时间制作这座雕像。

examples.src: She dreams of becoming a famous sculptor.
examples.dst: 她梦想成为一名著名的雕塑家。

examples.src: The sculptor used marble to create the figure.
examples.dst: 雕塑家用大理石创作了这个人像。

confuse.diff: sculptor 指人；sculpture 指作品。

examples.src: We visited an art gallery on Sunday.
examples.dst: 星期天我们参观了一家美术馆。

examples.src: His paintings are shown in a gallery downtown.
examples.dst: 他的画在市中心的一家画廊展出。

examples.src: The gallery is free to enter for students.
examples.dst: 这家美术馆对学生免费开放。

confuse.diff: gallery 指画廊；galley 指(船上的)厨房。

examples.src: I have great faith in my teammates.
examples.dst: 我对我的队友们很有信心。

examples.src: She never lost faith in herself.
examples.dst: 她从未对自己失去信心。

examples.src: People of different faiths live in this city.
examples.dst: 这座城市里生活着信仰不同的人。

confuse.diff: faith 指信任、信仰；fate 指命运。

examples.src: He faithfully followed the doctor's advice.
examples.dst: 他忠实地遵照医生的建议。

examples.src: The dog waited faithfully for its owner.
examples.dst: 那条狗忠实地等着它的主人。

examples.src: The film faithfully follows the original novel.
examples.dst: 这部电影忠实于原著小说。

confuse.diff: faithfully 是副词；faithful 是形容词，意为忠实的。

examples.src: He didn't study hard; consequently, he failed the exam.
examples.dst: 他没有努力学习，因此考试没及格。

examples.src: The road was closed and consequently we were late.
examples.dst: 道路被封了，因此我们迟到了。

examples.src: She missed the bus and consequently missed the meeting.
examples.dst: 她错过了公交车，因此错过了会议。

confuse.diff: consequently 强调因果；subsequently 强调时间上随后。

examples.src: My aim is to become a doctor.
examples.dst: 我的目标是成为一名医生。

examples.src: He aimed the ball at the basket and shot.
examples.dst: 他瞄准篮筐投出了球。

examples.src: The project aims to protect wild animals.
examples.dst: 这个项目旨在保护野生动物。

confuse.diff: aim 指目标、瞄准；arm 指手臂或武装。

examples.src: She prefers conventional methods of teaching.
examples.dst: 她更喜欢传统的教学方法。

examples.src: The artist broke away from conventional styles.
examples.dst: 这位艺术家摆脱了传统风格。

examples.src: Conventional energy sources are running out.
examples.dst: 传统能源正在枯竭。

confuse.diff: conventional 是形容词；convention 是名词，指惯例或大会。

examples.src: This is a typical English breakfast.
examples.dst: 这是一份典型的英式早餐。

examples.src: It is typical of him to arrive late.
examples.dst: 迟到是他一贯的作风。

examples.src: A typical day for her begins at six.
examples.dst: 她典型的一天从六点开始。

confuse.diff: typical 指典型的；topical 指时事的、热门话题的。

examples.src: It was evident that she had been crying.
examples.dst: 很明显她刚才哭过。

examples.src: His joy was evident to everyone in the room.
examples.dst: 屋里每个人都看得出他的喜悦。

examples.src: The improvement in his grades is evident.
examples.dst: 他成绩的进步很明显。

confuse.diff: evident 是形容词，意为明显的；evidence 是名词，意为证据。

examples.src: The town is enjoying a cultural renaissance.
examples.dst: 这座小镇正在经历文化复兴。

examples.src: Poetry has seen a renaissance in recent years.
examples.dst: 近年来诗歌迎来了复兴。

examples.src: The city's renaissance began with new investment.
examples.dst: 这座城市的复兴始于新的投资。

confuse.diff: renaissance 指复兴；resistance 指抵抗。

examples.src: The Renaissance began in Italy in the 14th century.
examples.dst: 文艺复兴于14世纪始于意大利。

examples.src: Leonardo da Vinci was a great figure of the Renaissance.
examples.dst: 达·芬奇是文艺复兴时期的伟大人物。

examples.src: Many famous paintings come from the Renaissance.
examples.dst: 许多著名的画作来自文艺复兴时期。

confuse.diff: the Renaissance 特指历史上的文艺复兴；renaissance 泛指复兴。

examples.src: The school adopted a new way of teaching.
examples.dst: 学校采用了一种新的教学方法。

examples.src: They adopted a baby girl last year.
examples.dst: 他们去年收养了一个女婴。

examples.src: The committee adopted our suggestion.
examples.dst: 委员会采纳了我们的建议。

confuse.diff: adopt 指采用、收养；adapt 指适应、改编。

means: 人文主义的；人道主义的

examples.src: The school takes a humanistic approach to education.
examples.dst: 这所学校采取人文主义的教育方式。

examples.src: Renaissance art has a strong humanistic spirit.
examples.dst: 文艺复兴艺术具有浓厚的人文主义精神。

examples.src: He admired the humanistic values in the novel.
examples.dst: 他欣赏这部小说中的人文价值观。

confuse.diff: humanistic 指人文主义的；humane 指仁慈的、人道的。

examples.src: She possesses a great talent for music.
examples.dst: 她拥有出色的音乐天赋。

examples.src: He doesn't possess a car.
examples.dst: 他没有汽车。

examples.src: The museum possesses many rare books.
examples.dst: 这家博物馆拥有许多珍本书籍。

confuse.diff: possess 是动词；possession 是名词，指拥有物。

examples.src: He lost all his possessions in the fire.
examples.dst: 他在火灾中失去了所有财物。

examples.src: The police found drugs in his possession.
examples.dst: 警察在他身上发现了毒品。

examples.src: Her most precious possession is an old photo.
examples.dst: 她最珍贵的财物是一张旧照片。

confuse.diff: possession 是名词；possess 是动词。

examples.src: The pianist gave a superb performance.
examples.dst: 这位钢琴家的演奏极为出色。

examples.src: We had a superb view of the mountains.
examples.dst: 我们看到了壮丽的山景。

examples.src: The food at that restaurant is superb.
examples.dst: 那家餐厅的食物棒极了。

confuse.diff: superb 指极好的；super 是口语里的“超级好”，也可作前缀。

examples.src: Try to see the problem from a different perspective.
examples.dst: 试着从不同的角度看这个问题。

examples.src: Travelling gave him a new perspective on life.
examples.dst: 旅行给了他看待生活的新视角。

examples.src: The artist used perspective to create depth.
examples.dst: 这位艺术家运用透视法营造出纵深感。

confuse.diff: perspective 指视角；prospective 指预期的、未来的。

examples.src: She learned a new painting technique.
examples.dst: 她学了一种新的绘画技巧。

examples.src: This technique helps you remember words faster.
examples.dst: 这个方法能帮你更快地记单词。

examples.src: The singer has excellent vocal technique.
examples.dst: 这位歌手有出色的发声技巧。

confuse.diff: technique 指具体技巧；technology 指科技。

examples.src: It was pure coincidence that we met at the airport.
examples.dst: 我们在机场相遇纯属巧合。

examples.src: What a coincidence! We have the same birthday.
examples.dst: 真巧！我们生日是同一天。

examples.src: The two events happening together was no coincidence.
examples.dst: 两件事同时发生并非巧合。

confuse.diff: coincidence 是名词，指巧合；coincide 是动词，指同时发生、一致。

examples.src: By coincidence, we were on the same train.
examples.dst: 碰巧，我们坐的是同一列火车。

examples.src: I found the book by coincidence.
examples.dst: 我碰巧找到了这本书。

examples.src: They met by coincidence in a small café.
examples.dst: 他们在一家小咖啡馆里偶然相遇。

confuse.diff: by coincidence 强调事情巧合；by accident 强调非故意。

examples.src: The Mona Lisa is a masterpiece of Renaissance art.
examples.dst: 《蒙娜丽莎》是文艺复兴艺术的杰作。

examples.src: This novel is regarded as his masterpiece.
examples.dst: 这部小说被视为他的代表作。

examples.src: The museum holds many masterpieces.
examples.dst: 这家博物馆收藏了许多杰作。

confuse.diff: masterpiece 指杰作；mastermind 指策划者、幕后主脑。

examples.src: Impressionism began in France in the 19th century.
examples.dst: 印象派于19世纪始于法国。

examples.src: She wrote a paper on impressionism.
examples.dst: 她写了一篇关于印象派的论文。

examples.src: Impressionism focuses on light and colour.
examples.dst: 印象派注重光与色彩。

confuse.diff: impressionism 指印象派；impression 指印象。

examples.src: Monet was a famous impressionist.
examples.dst: 莫奈是一位著名的印象派画家。

examples.src: We saw an impressionist exhibition in Paris.
examples.dst: 我们在巴黎看了一场印象派画展。

examples.src: The impressionist style uses short brush strokes.
examples.dst: 印象派风格使用短促的笔触。

confuse.diff: impressionist 指画家或印象派的；impressionism 指这一流派。

examples.src: Van Gogh was a great post-impressionist.
examples.dst: 梵高是一位伟大的后印象派画家。

examples.src: The gallery has a post-impressionist collection.
examples.dst: 这家美术馆有一批后印象派的藏品。

examples.src: Post-impressionist painters used bold colours.
examples.dst: 后印象派画家使用大胆的色彩。

confuse.diff: post-impressionist 是后印象派；impressionist 是印象派。

examples.src: He spent a great deal of time on the project.
examples.dst: 他在这个项目上花了大量时间。

examples.src: I learned a great deal from my grandfather.
examples.dst: 我从爷爷那里学到了很多。

examples.src: She cares a great deal about the environment.
examples.dst: 她非常关心环境。

confuse.diff: 两者意思接近；a great deal 程度更强。

examples.src: The tree cast a long shadow on the grass.
examples.dst: 这棵树在草地上投下长长的影子。

examples.src: The child hid in the shadow of the wall.
examples.dst: 孩子躲在墙的阴影里。

examples.src: A detective shadowed the suspect for days.
examples.dst: 一名侦探连续几天跟踪这名嫌疑人。

confuse.diff: shadow 指物体投下的影子；shade 指阴凉处。

examples.src: It's ridiculous to pay so much for a pen.
examples.dst: 为一支笔付这么多钱太荒唐了。

examples.src: He looked ridiculous in that big hat.
examples.dst: 他戴着那顶大帽子看起来很可笑。

examples.src: What a ridiculous idea!
examples.dst: 多么荒谬的想法！

confuse.diff: ridiculous 是形容词；ridicule 是动词或名词，意为嘲笑。

examples.src: The new law is very controversial.
examples.dst: 这项新法律很有争议。

examples.src: They had a controversial discussion about school uniforms.
examples.dst: 他们就校服问题展开了一场争议不小的讨论。

examples.src: The artist is known for his controversial works.
examples.dst: 这位艺术家以其有争议的作品而闻名。

confuse.diff: controversial 是形容词；controversy 是名词，指争论。

examples.src: He attempted to climb the mountain alone.
examples.dst: 他试图独自爬上这座山。

examples.src: It was her third attempt to pass the test.
examples.dst: 这是她第三次尝试通过测试。

examples.src: The first attempt failed, but they didn't give up.
examples.dst: 第一次尝试失败了，但他们没有放弃。

confuse.diff: attempt 指尝试；tempt 指引诱。

examples.src: The job is well paid; on the other hand, it is very tiring.
examples.dst: 这份工作报酬不错，但另一方面也很累人。

examples.src: Living in a city is convenient. On the other hand, it can be noisy.
examples.dst: 住在城市很方便，但另一方面也可能很吵。

examples.src: I like the plan, but, on the other hand, it costs too much.
examples.dst: 我喜欢这个计划，但另一方面它太贵了。

confuse.diff: on the one hand 引出第一个方面；on the other hand 引出对立的另一方面。

examples.src: No one can predict the weather exactly.
examples.dst: 没有人能准确预测天气。

examples.src: Experts predict that prices will rise next year.
examples.dst: 专家预测明年物价会上涨。

examples.src: It is hard to predict who will win the game.
examples.dst: 很难预测谁会赢得比赛。

confuse.diff: predict 指预测；predicate 指谓语或断言。

examples.src: The landscape here is beautiful in autumn.
examples.dst: 这里的秋色风景十分优美。

examples.src: He painted a landscape of the lake.
examples.dst: 他画了一幅湖景图。

examples.src: Wind farms have changed the landscape of the area.
examples.dst: 风力发电场改变了这个地区的景观。

confuse.diff: landscape 指一片土地的景观；scenery 泛指风景，不可数。

examples.src: Can you give me a specific example?
examples.dst: 你能给我举个具体的例子吗？

examples.src: She has a specific reason for coming here.
examples.dst: 她来这里有特定的原因。

examples.src: This medicine is for a specific disease.
examples.dst: 这种药是针对某种特定疾病的。

confuse.diff: specific 指具体的、特定的；special 指特别的。

examples.src: The figures show that sales have gone up.
examples.dst: 数据显示销量已经上升。

examples.src: Lu Xun is a great figure in modern Chinese literature.
examples.dst: 鲁迅是中国现代文学中的伟大人物。

examples.src: I figure we should leave before it gets dark.
examples.dst: 我认为我们应该在天黑前离开。

confuse.diff: figure 指数字、人物、身材；finger 指手指。

examples.src: The children made little animals out of clay.
examples.dst: 孩子们用黏土做了小动物。

examples.src: These pots are made of red clay.
examples.dst: 这些罐子是用红陶土做的。

examples.src: The ground here is heavy clay.
examples.dst: 这里的土壤是很黏的黏土。

confuse.diff: clay 指黏土；clean 指干净的、清洁。

examples.src: The film critic gave the movie five stars.
examples.dst: 这位影评人给这部电影打了五星。

examples.src: Critics praised the new play.
examples.dst: 评论家们称赞了这部新戏剧。

examples.src: He is a strong critic of the government's plan.
examples.dst: 他强烈批评政府的计划。

confuse.diff: critic 指评论者；critique 指评论文章或评论行为。

examples.src: The statue is made of bronze.
examples.dst: 这座雕像是青铜制成的。

examples.src: She won a bronze medal in swimming.
examples.dst: 她在游泳比赛中赢得了一枚铜牌。

examples.src: The museum has many ancient bronzes.
examples.dst: 这家博物馆有许多古代青铜器。

confuse.diff: bronze 是青铜(铜锡合金)；brass 是黄铜(铜锌合金)。

examples.src: The floor of the hall is made of white marble.
examples.dst: 大厅的地面是白色大理石铺的。

examples.src: The sculptor carved a horse out of marble.
examples.dst: 雕塑家用大理石雕出了一匹马。

examples.src: The boys played marbles in the yard.
examples.dst: 男孩们在院子里玩弹珠。

confuse.diff: marble 指大理石；marvel 指奇迹或感到惊叹。

examples.src: He carved a bird out of wood.
examples.dst: 他用木头刻了一只鸟。

examples.src: Their names were carved on the tree.
examples.dst: 他们的名字被刻在树上。

examples.src: Father carved the turkey at dinner.
examples.dst: 父亲在晚餐时切了火鸡。

confuse.diff: carve 指雕刻；curve 指曲线或弯曲。

examples.src: The vase is too delicate to carry in a bag.
examples.dst: 这只花瓶太易碎，不能放在包里带。

examples.src: She wore a delicate silver necklace.
examples.dst: 她戴着一条精致的银项链。

examples.src: This is a delicate matter and needs care.
examples.dst: 这是个微妙的问题，需要谨慎处理。

confuse.diff: delicate 指精致的、脆弱的；delicious 指美味的。

examples.src: The tent is made of heavy canvas.
examples.dst: 这顶帐篷由厚帆布制成。

examples.src: The artist stretched a new canvas on the frame.
examples.dst: 艺术家在画框上绷了一块新画布。

examples.src: She bought a pair of canvas shoes.
examples.dst: 她买了一双帆布鞋。

confuse.diff: canvas 指帆布、画布；canvass 指拉选票、游说。

examples.src: We had lunch in a small café near the school.
examples.dst: 我们在学校附近的一家小咖啡馆吃了午饭。

examples.src: She works part-time in a café.
examples.dst: 她在一家咖啡馆做兼职。

examples.src: Let's meet at the café at four.
examples.dst: 我们四点在咖啡馆见面吧。

confuse.diff: café 指咖啡馆；cafeteria 指自助食堂。

examples.src: I am allergic to peanuts.
examples.dst: 我对花生过敏。

examples.src: He had an allergic reaction to the medicine.
examples.dst: 他对这种药产生了过敏反应。

examples.src: She is allergic to cats and dust.
examples.dst: 她对猫和灰尘过敏。

confuse.diff: allergic 是形容词；allergy 是名词，指过敏症。

examples.src: She used her time effectively.
examples.dst: 她有效地利用了时间。

examples.src: The new method works effectively.
examples.dst: 这种新方法很有效。

examples.src: The two companies have effectively become one.
examples.dst: 这两家公司实际上已经合二为一。

confuse.diff: effectively 强调效果；efficiently 强调效率，少耗时耗力。

examples.src: We went to an art exhibition last weekend.
examples.dst: 上周末我们去看了一场艺术展。

examples.src: The exhibition opens on Monday.
examples.dst: 展览周一开幕。

examples.src: His photos are on exhibition in the library.
examples.dst: 他的照片正在图书馆展出。

confuse.diff: exhibition 指展览会；exhibit 指展品，也可作动词，意为展出。

examples.src: The dog became aggressive when strangers came near.
examples.dst: 陌生人靠近时，那条狗变得具有攻击性。

examples.src: He is an aggressive player who never gives up.
examples.dst: 他是一名积极进取、从不放弃的球员。

examples.src: Aggressive behaviour is not allowed at school.
examples.dst: 学校不允许有攻击性的行为。

confuse.diff: aggressive 是形容词；aggression 是名词，指侵略、攻击。

examples.src: He is a famous scholar of ancient history.
examples.dst: 他是一位著名的古代史学者。

examples.src: Many scholars attended the conference.
examples.dst: 许多学者参加了这次会议。

examples.src: She became a Rhodes scholar at twenty.
examples.dst: 她二十岁时成为罗德奖学金获得者。

confuse.diff: scholar 指学者；scholarship 指奖学金或学问。

examples.src: The knife cut deep into his flesh.
examples.dst: 刀深深地割进了他的肉里。

examples.src: The flesh of this fruit is sweet and soft.
examples.dst: 这种水果的果肉又甜又软。

examples.src: Some animals eat only flesh.
examples.dst: 有些动物只吃肉。

confuse.diff: flesh 指肉；flash 指闪光、闪现。

examples.src: I finally saw my favourite singer in the flesh.
examples.dst: 我终于见到了我最喜欢的歌手本人。

examples.src: She looks much younger in the flesh than on TV.
examples.dst: 她本人看起来比电视上年轻得多。

examples.src: It was exciting to meet the author in the flesh.
examples.dst: 亲眼见到这位作者令人兴奋。

confuse.diff: 两者都指亲自；in the flesh 多用于见到名人本人。

examples.src: We learn geometry in maths class.
examples.dst: 我们在数学课上学习几何。

examples.src: The building is famous for its beautiful geometry.
examples.dst: 这座建筑以其优美的几何造型而闻名。

examples.src: She is good at solving geometry problems.
examples.dst: 她擅长解几何题。

confuse.diff: geometry 指几何；geography 指地理。

examples.src: He gave her a bunch of roses.
examples.dst: 他送给她一束玫瑰。

examples.src: I bought a bunch of grapes at the market.
examples.dst: 我在市场上买了一串葡萄。

examples.src: A bunch of students were waiting outside.

examples.src: Fifth Avenue is famous for its shops.

examples.dst: 他们沿着一条林荫大道走下去。

examples.dst: 请告诉我们你的饮食偏好。

examples.dst: 本地学生将享有优先权。

confuse.diff: preference 指偏爱；reference 指参考、提及。

examples.dst: 纽约的古根海姆博物馆采用螺旋形设计。

examples.dst: 我们在古根海姆博物馆待了整整一下午。

examples.dst: 古根海姆博物馆收藏现代艺术作品。

confuse.diff: Guggenheim Museum 以现代艺术为主；Metropolitan Museum 是综合性大都会艺术博物馆。

examples.src: The shop displays its new clothes in the window.
examples.dst: 商店把新款衣服陈列在橱窗里。

examples.src: The children's drawings are on display in the hall.
examples.dst: 孩子们的画正在大厅里展出。

examples.src: The screen displays the time and date.
examples.dst: 屏幕上显示着时间和日期。

confuse.diff: display 指展示；disclose 指透露、公开(秘密)。

examples.src: The film has a wide appeal for young people.
examples.dst: 这部电影对年轻人很有吸引力。

examples.src: The police made an appeal for information.
examples.dst: 警方呼吁提供线索。

examples.src: He appealed against the court's decision.
examples.dst: 他对法院的判决提出了上诉。

confuse.diff: appeal 指吸引、呼吁；appear 指出现、似乎。

examples.src: The idea appeals to many young people.
examples.dst: 这个想法对许多年轻人有吸引力。

examples.src: The mayor appealed to citizens to save water.
examples.dst: 市长呼吁市民节约用水。

examples.src: Sweet food doesn't appeal to me.
examples.dst: 甜食对我没有吸引力。

confuse.diff: appeal to 指吸引、呼吁；apply to 指适用于、向…申请。

examples.src: Be careful with the box. It contains fragile glasses.
examples.dst: 小心这个箱子，里面是易碎的玻璃杯。

examples.src: The old man's health is very fragile.
examples.dst: 这位老人的身体很虚弱。

examples.src: Peace in the region remains fragile.
examples.dst: 这个地区的和平依然脆弱。

confuse.diff: fragile 指易碎的；fragrant 指芳香的。

examples.dst: 房间中间有一张圆桌。

examples.dst: 他们沿着湖边环形步行了一圈。

examples.src: The school sent a circular to all parents.
examples.dst: 学校给所有家长发了一份通知。

confuse.diff: circular 是形容词；circle 是名词，指圆或圈。

examples.src: The metropolitan area has over ten million people.
examples.dst: 这个大都市地区有一千多万人口。

examples.src: He works at the Metropolitan Museum of Art.
examples.dst: 他在大都会艺术博物馆工作。

examples.src: Metropolitan life can be fast and stressful.
examples.dst: 大都市的生活节奏可能很快，压力也大。

confuse.diff: metropolitan 指大都市的；cosmopolitan 指国际化的、世界性的。

examples.src: The restaurant has a good reputation for its fish.
examples.dst: 这家餐厅的鱼很有名。

examples.src: He worked hard to build his reputation.
examples.dst: 他努力树立自己的声誉。

examples.src: One mistake can ruin your reputation.
examples.dst: 一次错误就可能毁掉你的名誉。

confuse.diff: reputation 指名誉；repetition 指重复。

examples.src: Ancient Egypt had a great civilization.
examples.dst: 古埃及拥有伟大的文明。

examples.dst: 黄河是中华文明的摇篮。

examples.src: Modern civilization depends on science and technology.
examples.dst: 现代文明依赖科学技术。

confuse.diff: civilization 指文明；civilian 指平民。

examples.src: Pictures help make the lesson more visual.
examples.dst: 图片使这节课更加直观。

examples.src: He has a good visual memory.
examples.dst: 他的视觉记忆很好。

examples.src: The film is a visual treat.
examples.dst: 这部电影在视觉上令人享受。

confuse.diff: visual 指视觉的；visible 指看得见的。

examples.src: The garden is full of fragrant flowers.
examples.dst: 花园里满是芬芳的花朵。

examples.src: A fragrant smell came from the kitchen.
examples.dst: 厨房里飘来一股香味。

examples.src: She drank a cup of fragrant tea.
examples.dst: 她喝了一杯清香的茶。

confuse.diff: fragrant 指芳香的；fragile 指易碎的。

examples.dst: 麦迪逊大道以其广告公司而闻名。

examples.src: James Madison was the fourth President of the United States.
examples.dst: 詹姆斯·麦迪逊是美国第四任总统。

examples.src: Madison is the capital of Wisconsin.
examples.dst: 麦迪逊是威斯康星州的首府。

confuse.diff: Madison 是姓氏或地名；Madeline 是女子名。

examples.src: She likes contemporary music and art.
examples.dst: 她喜欢当代音乐和艺术。

examples.src: Shakespeare and Marlowe were contemporaries.
examples.dst: 莎士比亚和马洛是同时代的人。

examples.src: The museum has a contemporary art section.
examples.dst: 博物馆设有当代艺术展区。

confuse.diff: contemporary 指当代的；temporary 指暂时的。

examples.src: She is looking for a permanent job.
examples.dst: 她在找一份固定工作。

examples.src: The accident left a permanent scar on his arm.
examples.dst: 那次事故在他手臂上留下了永久的疤痕。

examples.src: The museum has a permanent collection and special shows.
examples.dst: 博物馆有常设展品，也有特别展览。

confuse.diff: permanent 指永久的；permit 指允许或许可证。

examples.dst: 他们住在城里一个安静的区域。

examples.dst: 海淀区有很多大学。

examples.src: The shopping district is crowded at weekends.
examples.dst: 购物区在周末很拥挤。

confuse.diff: district 指地区；distinct 指明显不同的。

confuse.diff: committee 指委员会；commission 指佣金、委托或官方调查委员会。

examples.src: Please put your signature at the bottom of the form.
examples.dst: 请在表格底部签名。

examples.dst: 这位歌手在一张照片上给我签了名。

examples.dst: 亮红色外套是她标志性的风格。

confuse.diff: signature 指签名；sign 指标志、记号或签署。

examples.dst: 他年轻时写过诗。

examples.dst: 她跳舞的样子富有诗意。

confuse.diff: poetry 是不可数的诗歌总称；poem 是一首具体的诗。

examples.src: This poem has no rhyme.
examples.dst: 这首诗不押韵。

confuse.diff: rhyme 指韵脚；rhythm 指节奏。

examples.src: Words cannot convey how happy I am.

confuse.diff: convey 指传达、运送；convince 指使信服。

examples.dst: 这扇门是自动的，会自己打开。

examples.dst: 眨眼是一种本能反应。

examples.dst: 她买了一辆自动挡的车。

confuse.diff: automatically 是副词；automatic 是形容词。

examples.src: Exercise is good for mental health.

examples.src: He did the sum by mental arithmetic.

examples.dst: 她承受着很大的精神压力。

examples.dst: 她在心里为演讲做准备。

examples.src: The job was mentally tiring.
examples.dst: 这份工作让人精神疲惫。

confuse.diff: mentally 是副词；mental 是形容词。

examples.dst: 我父亲去年戒烟了。

examples.src: She quit her job to travel the world.
examples.dst: 她辞掉工作去环游世界。

examples.dst: 没试之前不要放弃。

examples.src: The medicine took effect in an hour.
examples.dst: 这药一小时后见效了。

examples.dst: 这部电影的特效很惊人。

confuse.diff: effect 多为名词，指影响；affect 多为动词，意为影响。

examples.src: Smoking can damage your lungs.
examples.dst: 吸烟会损害你的肺。

examples.dst: 他深吸一口气，让空气充满肺部。

examples.src: The doctor listened to her lungs.
examples.dst: 医生听了听她的肺部。

confuse.diff: lung 指肺；long 指长的。

examples.dst: 她怀孕五个月了。

examples.src: Pregnant women should not smoke.
examples.dst: 孕妇不应该吸烟。

examples.src: My sister is pregnant with her second child.
examples.dst: 我姐姐怀上了第二个孩子。

confuse.diff: pregnant 是形容词；pregnancy 是名词，指怀孕。

examples.src: The test showed abnormal heart activity.
examples.dst: 检查显示心脏活动异常。

examples.src: It is abnormal for it to be this hot in spring.
examples.dst: 春天这么热不正常。

examples.src: The dog's abnormal behaviour worried us.
examples.dst: 那条狗的反常行为让我们担心。

confuse.diff: abnormal 指反常的；normal 指正常的。

means: 气喘吁吁的；呼吸困难的

examples.src: He was breathless after running up the stairs.
examples.dst: 他跑上楼梯后气喘吁吁。

examples.src: She arrived breathless and red in the face.
examples.dst: 她气喘吁吁、满脸通红地赶到了。

examples.src: The audience watched in breathless silence.
examples.dst: 观众屏息静静地观看。

confuse.diff: breathless 是形容词，意为喘不过气的；breathe 是动词，意为呼吸。

means: 不健康的；身体状况差的

examples.src: I'm unfit because I never exercise.
examples.dst: 我从不锻炼，所以身体状况不好。

examples.src: The food was unfit to eat.
examples.dst: 这食物不适合食用。

examples.src: He was judged unfit for the job.
examples.dst: 他被认为不适合这份工作。

confuse.diff: unfit 指不健康、不适合；unfair 指不公平的。

examples.src: Swimming strengthens your muscles.
examples.dst: 游泳能增强你的肌肉。

examples.src: The two countries want to strengthen their ties.
examples.dst: 两国希望加强彼此的联系。

examples.src: The wind strengthened during the night.
examples.dst: 夜里风力变强了。

confuse.diff: strengthen 是动词；strength 是名词，指力量。

examples.src: She resolved to study harder this term.
examples.dst: 她下决心这学期更加努力学习。

examples.src: The two sides resolved their differences.
examples.dst: 双方化解了分歧。

examples.src: His resolve to quit smoking was strong.
examples.dst: 他戒烟的决心很坚定。

confuse.diff: resolve 是动词或表决心；resolution 是名词，指决议、分辨率。

examples.src: We decided on a date for the party.
examples.dst: 我们选定了聚会的日期。

examples.src: Have you decided on a name for the baby?
examples.dst: 你们给宝宝选好名字了吗？

examples.src: She decided on the blue dress.
examples.dst: 她选定了那件蓝色连衣裙。

confuse.diff: decide on 后接名词，指选定；decide to 后接动词，指决定做某事。

examples.src: He bought a packet of biscuits.
examples.dst: 他买了一包饼干。

examples.dst: 我包里有一包纸巾。

examples.src: Data is sent over the network in packets.
examples.dst: 数据以数据包的形式在网络上传输。

confuse.diff: packet 指小包；pocket 指口袋。

examples.dst: 我想喝杯茶。

examples.src: It feels like spring today.

examples.dst: 你今晚想出去吗？

confuse.diff: feel like 指感觉像或想要；look like 指看起来像。

examples.dst: 我现在不想做作业。

examples.dst: 听到这个消息，她想哭。

examples.src: Do you feel like going for a walk?
examples.dst: 你想去散步吗？

confuse.diff: feel like doing 后接动名词；would like to do 后接动词不定式。

examples.src: After work he needs some relaxation.
examples.dst: 下班后他需要放松一下。

examples.src: Yoga helps with relaxation and sleep.
examples.dst: 瑜伽有助于放松和睡眠。

confuse.diff: relaxation 是名词，指放松；relaxed 是形容词，意为放松的。

examples.dst: 迷路的徒步者急需帮助。

examples.src: He made a desperate attempt to escape.
examples.dst: 他拼命想要逃脱。

examples.src: She felt desperate when she lost her job.
examples.dst: 失业时她感到绝望。

confuse.diff: desperate 指绝望的；separate 指分开的。

examples.dst: 这位化学家在研究实验室工作。

examples.dst: 我在药店买了些药。

examples.dst: 药剂师讲解了药片的服用方法。

confuse.diff: chemist 指化学家或药剂师；chemistry 指化学。

examples.dst: 不要把口香糖粘在课桌下面。

examples.dst: 刷牙有助于保持牙龈健康。

examples.dst: 邮票是用胶水粘上的。

confuse.diff: gum 指口香糖、牙龈；gun 指枪。

examples.dst: 她紧张时会嚼口香糖。

confuse.diff: chewing gum 是普通口香糖；bubble gum 是可以吹泡泡的泡泡糖。

examples.src: I was disappointed with the test result.

examples.dst: 旅行取消时她显得很失望。

examples.dst: 她的父母对她的放弃感到失望。

confuse.diff: disappointed 指人感到失望；disappointing 指令人失望的。

examples.dst: 疾病使他变得非常虚弱。

examples.dst: 风暴向内陆移动时减弱了。

examples.src: Too much sugar can weaken your teeth.
examples.dst: 糖吃多了会损害牙齿。

confuse.diff: weaken 指削弱；weekend 指周末。

examples.src: She was ashamed to tell the truth.
examples.dst: 她羞于说出真相。

confuse.diff: ashamed 指人感到羞愧；shameful 指事情可耻。

examples.src: We practised reading comprehension in class.
examples.dst: 我们在课堂上练习了阅读理解。

examples.src: The child has a good comprehension of numbers.
examples.dst: 这个孩子对数字的理解力很强。

confuse.diff: comprehension 指理解；compression 指压缩。

confuse.diff: in spite of 后接名词或动名词；后者引导从句。

examples.dst: 做生意要成功就得冒险。

examples.dst: 雪天开车不要冒险。

confuse.diff: take risks 指多次或泛指冒险；take a risk 指一次冒险。

examples.dst: 有时你必须冒一次险。

examples.dst: 我不会拿自己的健康冒险。

confuse.diff: take a risk 强调一次；take risks 泛指经常冒险。

confuse.diff: disco 指迪斯科舞厅；disk 指磁盘或圆盘。

examples.src: Abortion is a controversial topic in many countries.
examples.dst: 在许多国家，堕胎是个有争议的话题。

examples.src: The law on abortion has changed.
examples.dst: 关于堕胎的法律已经改变。

examples.src: They discussed the ethics of abortion.
examples.dst: 他们讨论了堕胎的伦理问题。

confuse.diff: abortion 指堕胎；abortive 指失败的、夭折的。

examples.src: The old man smoked a cigar after dinner.
examples.dst: 老人饭后抽了一支雪茄。

examples.src: He gave his friend a box of cigars.
examples.dst: 他送给朋友一盒雪茄。

examples.src: The room smelled of cigar smoke.
examples.dst: 房间里有雪茄烟味。

confuse.diff: cigar 是雪茄；cigarette 是香烟。

examples.src: She felt embarrassed when she forgot his name.
examples.dst: 她忘了他的名字，感到很尴尬。

examples.src: He was too embarrassed to ask for help.
examples.dst: 他不好意思求助。

examples.src: I was embarrassed by my mistake.
examples.dst: 我为自己的错误感到难堪。

confuse.diff: embarrassed 指人感到尴尬；embarrassing 指令人尴尬的。

examples.src: There was an awkward silence in the room.
examples.dst: 房间里出现了尴尬的沉默。

examples.src: He felt awkward at the party.
examples.dst: 他在聚会上感到很不自在。

examples.src: The box is awkward to carry.
examples.dst: 这个箱子很不好搬。

confuse.diff: awkward 指尴尬的、笨拙的；backward 指向后的、落后的。

examples.src: This car consumes a lot of petrol.
examples.dst: 这辆车很耗油。

examples.src: Teenagers consume a lot of fast food.
examples.dst: 青少年吃很多快餐。

examples.src: The project consumed all her time.
examples.dst: 这个项目占用了她所有的时间。

confuse.diff: consume 指消耗；assume 指假定。

examples.src: Wind and solar power are renewable energy.
examples.dst: 风能和太阳能是可再生能源。

examples.src: The country plans to use more renewable resources.
examples.dst: 这个国家计划更多地使用可再生资源。

examples.src: The contract is renewable every year.
examples.dst: 该合同每年可续签。

confuse.diff: renewable 是形容词；renewal 是名词，指更新、续订。

examples.src: They grow tomatoes in a greenhouse.
examples.dst: 他们在温室里种番茄。

examples.src: The greenhouse effect is making the earth warmer.
examples.dst: 温室效应使地球变暖。

examples.src: Greenhouse gases come from burning fuel.
examples.dst: 温室气体来自燃料燃烧。

confuse.diff: greenhouse 连写指温室；green house 分写指绿色的房子。

examples.src: Water freezes at 32 degrees Fahrenheit.
examples.dst: 水在华氏32度时结冰。

examples.src: It was 90 degrees Fahrenheit yesterday.
examples.dst: 昨天是华氏90度。

examples.src: The United States uses the Fahrenheit scale.
examples.dst: 美国使用华氏温标。

confuse.diff: Fahrenheit 是华氏；Celsius 是摄氏。

examples.src: How did the accident come about?
examples.dst: 这起事故是怎么发生的？

examples.src: The change came about slowly.
examples.dst: 这一变化是慢慢发生的。

examples.src: I don't know how the argument came about.
examples.dst: 我不知道这场争吵是怎么起的。

confuse.diff: come about 指发生；come across 指偶然遇到。

examples.src: The graph shows how the temperature changed.
examples.dst: 这张图显示了温度的变化。

examples.src: She drew a graph of the test scores.
examples.dst: 她画了一张考试成绩曲线图。

examples.src: Look at the graph on page ten.
examples.dst: 请看第十页的图表。

confuse.diff: graph 指图表；grab 指抓取。

examples.src: The winners were chosen at random.
examples.dst: 获奖者是随机抽取的。

examples.src: The survey used a random sample of students.
examples.dst: 这项调查抽取了随机学生样本。

examples.src: He asked a few random questions.
examples.dst: 他随便问了几个问题。

confuse.diff: random 指随机的；ransom 指赎金。

examples.src: Rainbows are a natural phenomenon.
examples.dst: 彩虹是一种自然现象。

examples.src: Global warming is a worrying phenomenon.
examples.dst: 全球变暖是一种令人担忧的现象。

examples.src: Scientists study strange phenomena.
examples.dst: 科学家研究奇怪的现象。

confuse.diff: phenomenon 是单数；phenomena 是复数。

examples.src: I subscribe to a science magazine.
examples.dst: 我订阅了一份科学杂志。

examples.src: Click here to subscribe to our channel.
examples.dst: 点击这里订阅我们的频道。

examples.src: Many people subscribe to this view.
examples.dst: 许多人赞同这种看法。

confuse.diff: subscribe 指订阅；describe 指描述。

examples.src: She subscribes to several newspapers.
examples.dst: 她订阅了几份报纸。

examples.src: Have you subscribed to the newsletter?
examples.dst: 你订阅这份通讯了吗？

examples.src: I can't subscribe to that theory.
examples.dst: 我不能赞同那种理论。

confuse.diff: subscribe to 强调订阅的对象；subscribe 单用时多指订阅这一动作。

examples.src: The scientist found a dinosaur fossil.
examples.dst: 科学家发现了一块恐龙化石。

examples.src: Fossils tell us about ancient life.
examples.dst: 化石告诉我们远古生命的情况。

examples.src: Coal and oil are fossil fuels.
examples.dst: 煤和石油是化石燃料。

confuse.diff: fossil 指化石；fossil fuel 指化石燃料。

examples.src: The car ran out of fuel.
examples.dst: 汽车没油了。

examples.src: Wood is used as fuel in some villages.
examples.dst: 有些村子用木头作燃料。

examples.src: Rumours fuelled their fears.
examples.dst: 谣言加重了他们的恐惧。

confuse.diff: fuel 指燃料；feel 指感觉。

examples.src: Sawdust is a byproduct of making furniture.
examples.dst: 锯末是制作家具的副产品。

examples.src: Carbon dioxide is a byproduct of burning fuel.
examples.dst: 二氧化碳是燃烧燃料的副产物。

examples.src: Stress can be a byproduct of success.
examples.dst: 压力可能是成功的附带结果。

confuse.diff: byproduct 指副产品；product 指产品。

examples.src: Methane is a greenhouse gas.
examples.dst: 甲烷是一种温室气体。

examples.src: Farms produce methane from animal waste.
examples.dst: 农场的动物粪便会产生甲烷。

examples.src: Natural gas is mostly methane.
examples.dst: 天然气的主要成分是甲烷。

confuse.diff: methane 是甲烷；methanol 是甲醇。

examples.src: Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius.
examples.dst: 水在摄氏100度沸腾。

examples.src: It is twenty degrees Celsius outside.
examples.dst: 外面是摄氏二十度。

examples.src: China uses the Celsius scale.
examples.dst: 中国使用摄氏温标。

confuse.diff: Celsius 是摄氏；Fahrenheit 是华氏。

examples.src: The quantity of water in the tank is small.
examples.dst: 水箱里的水量很少。

examples.src: Quality is more important than quantity.
examples.dst: 质量比数量更重要。

examples.src: She bought a large quantity of rice.
examples.dst: 她买了大量的大米。

confuse.diff: quantity 指数量；quality 指质量。

examples.src: They drank quantities of water after the race.
examples.dst: 比赛后他们喝了大量的水。

examples.src: Factories produce quantities of waste.
examples.dst: 工厂产生大量废物。

examples.src: The shop sells quantities of fresh fruit.
examples.dst: 这家店出售大量新鲜水果。

confuse.diff: quantities of 表示大量；a quantity of 表示一定数量或大量。

examples.src: Prices tend to rise in summer.
examples.dst: 夏天物价往往上涨。

examples.src: He tends to forget names.
examples.dst: 他容易忘记名字。

examples.src: The nurse tended the wounded soldiers.
examples.dst: 护士照料着受伤的士兵。

confuse.diff: tend 指倾向、照料；attend 指出席、上(学)。

examples.src: The price of oil has gone up again.
examples.dst: 油价又涨了。

examples.src: The temperature will go up tomorrow.
examples.dst: 明天气温将升高。

examples.src: New buildings are going up everywhere.
examples.dst: 到处都在盖起新楼。

confuse.diff: go up 指上升；go down 指下降。

examples.src: The tailor took my measurements.
examples.dst: 裁缝给我量了尺寸。

examples.src: Accurate measurement is important in science.
examples.dst: 精确测量在科学中很重要。

examples.src: The measurements of the room are four by five metres.
examples.dst: 房间的尺寸是四米乘五米。

confuse.diff: measurement 是测量或尺寸；measure 是动词，意为测量，也指措施。

examples.src: The car goes 60 miles per hour.
examples.dst: 这辆车每小时行驶60英里。

examples.src: The tickets cost ten yuan per person.
examples.dst: 门票每人十元。

examples.src: He earns 200 yuan per day.
examples.dst: 他每天挣200元。

confuse.diff: per 指每；pro 指赞成或专业的。

examples.src: The scientists collected data from many sources.
examples.dst: 科学家们从多个来源收集数据。

examples.src: The data shows that sales have increased.
examples.dst: 数据显示销量增加了。

examples.src: All the data is stored on the computer.
examples.dst: 所有数据都存在电脑里。

confuse.diff: data 指数据；date 指日期。

examples.src: Heavy rain resulted in floods.
examples.dst: 大雨导致了洪水。

examples.src: Careless driving can result in accidents.
examples.dst: 粗心驾驶可能造成事故。

examples.src: The meeting resulted in a new plan.
examples.dst: 这次会议产生了一个新计划。

confuse.diff: result in 指导致某结果；result from 指由…引起。

examples.src: There is a trend towards smaller families.
examples.dst: 家庭规模有变小的趋势。

examples.src: Short hair is the latest trend.
examples.dst: 短发是最新的潮流。

examples.src: The data shows a downward trend.
examples.dst: 数据显示出下降趋势。

confuse.diff: trend 是名词；trendy 是形容词，意为时髦的。

examples.src: The earthquake was a terrible catastrophe.
examples.dst: 这次地震是一场可怕的灾难。

examples.src: Pollution could lead to an environmental catastrophe.
examples.dst: 污染可能引发环境灾难。

examples.src: The party was a catastrophe from start to finish.
examples.dst: 这次聚会从头到尾都是一场灾难。

confuse.diff: catastrophe 是名词；catastrophic 是形容词，意为灾难性的。

examples.src: The heavy rain caused a serious flood in the region.
examples.dst: 大雨在该地区引发了严重的洪灾。

examples.src: The river flooded the nearby villages last summer.
examples.dst: 去年夏天河水淹没了附近的村庄。

examples.src: Letters of thanks flooded into the office after the event.
examples.dst: 活动结束后，感谢信像潮水般涌入办公室。

confuse.diff: flood 是洪水；blood 是血液。

examples.src: The long drought destroyed most of the crops.
examples.dst: 长期的干旱毁掉了大部分庄稼。

examples.src: Farmers are suffering from the worst drought in decades.
examples.dst: 农民们正遭受几十年来最严重的旱灾。

examples.src: The government has taken measures to fight the drought.
examples.dst: 政府已采取措施抗击旱灾。

confuse.diff: drought 是干旱；draught 是穿堂风（英式拼写）。

examples.src: Millions of people died in the great famine.
examples.dst: 数百万人死于那场大饥荒。

examples.src: War and drought brought famine to the country.
examples.dst: 战争和干旱给这个国家带来了饥荒。

examples.src: Aid organizations are sending food to the famine area.
examples.dst: 救援组织正在向饥荒地区运送粮食。

confuse.diff: famine 是饥荒；fame 是名声。

examples.src: Many students oppose the new school rule.
examples.dst: 许多学生反对这项新校规。

examples.src: She strongly opposed the plan to cut down the forest.
examples.dst: 她强烈反对砍伐森林的计划。

examples.src: The two parties opposed each other in the debate.
examples.dst: 两党在辩论中互相对立。

confuse.diff: oppose 是反对；expose 是暴露、揭露。

examples.src: Her parents were opposed to the idea at first.
examples.dst: 起初她的父母反对这个想法。

examples.src: The two leaders hold completely opposed views.
examples.dst: 两位领导人持完全对立的观点。

examples.src: Those opposed to the plan should raise their hands.
examples.dst: 反对这项计划的人请举手。

confuse.diff: opposed 指反对的；opposite 指相反的、对面的。

examples.src: Most villagers are opposed to building a factory here.
examples.dst: 大多数村民反对在这里建工厂。

examples.src: I am opposed to using violence to solve problems.
examples.dst: 我反对用暴力解决问题。

examples.src: Why are you so opposed to my suggestion?
examples.dst: 你为什么如此反对我的建议？

confuse.diff: be opposed to 是反对；be opposite to 是与……相反或在……对面。

examples.src: The city has a mild climate all year round.
examples.dst: 这座城市全年气候温和。

examples.src: He suffered only a mild injury in the accident.
examples.dst: 他在事故中只受了轻伤。

examples.src: She spoke in a mild voice to calm the child.
examples.dst: 她用温和的声音安抚孩子。

confuse.diff: mild 是温和的；mind 是头脑或介意。

examples.src: Air pollution is a major environmental problem.
examples.dst: 空气污染是一个重大的环境问题。

examples.src: The school organized an environmental protection campaign.
examples.dst: 学校组织了一次环保活动。

examples.src: Environmental awareness has grown among young people.
examples.dst: 年轻人的环保意识不断增强。

confuse.diff: environmental 是形容词；environment 是名词，指环境。

means: 环保人士；环境保护论者

examples.src: Environmentalists called for stricter laws on pollution.
examples.dst: 环保人士呼吁制定更严格的污染法规。

examples.src: The young environmentalist gave a speech at the conference.
examples.dst: 这位年轻的环保人士在会议上发表了演讲。

examples.src: Many environmentalists oppose the building of the dam.
examples.dst: 许多环保人士反对修建这座大坝。

confuse.diff: environmentalist 是环保人士；environmental 是环境的。

examples.src: You must think about the consequences of your actions.
examples.dst: 你必须考虑自己行为的后果。

examples.src: The factory closed as a consequence of the economic crisis.
examples.dst: 由于经济危机，这家工厂倒闭了。

examples.src: Global warming has serious consequences for the planet.
examples.dst: 全球变暖对地球有严重影响。

confuse.diff: consequence 是后果；sequence 是顺序、一连串。

examples.src: The old building is in a poor state.
examples.dst: 这栋老建筑的状况很差。

examples.src: California is the most populous state in the United States.
examples.dst: 加利福尼亚是美国人口最多的州。

examples.src: Please state your name and address clearly.
examples.dst: 请清楚地说明你的姓名和地址。

confuse.diff: state 指状态或国家；status 指地位、身份。

examples.src: The shop offers a wide range of products.
examples.dst: 这家商店提供种类繁多的商品。

examples.src: The students range in age from fifteen to eighteen.
examples.dst: 这些学生的年龄在十五岁到十八岁之间。

examples.src: The Alps are a famous mountain range in Europe.
examples.dst: 阿尔卑斯山是欧洲著名的山脉。

confuse.diff: range 是范围；arrange 是安排、整理。

examples.src: Even if it rains tomorrow, we will still go hiking.
examples.dst: 即使明天下雨，我们也会去远足。

examples.src: I will support you even if everyone else disagrees.
examples.dst: 即使其他人都不同意，我也会支持你。

examples.src: Even if you fail, you should not give up.
examples.dst: 即使失败了，你也不应该放弃。

confuse.diff: even if 表示假设的情况；even though 表示已经存在的事实。

examples.src: Keep on trying and you will succeed.
examples.dst: 坚持尝试，你会成功的。

examples.src: He kept on talking although nobody was listening.
examples.dst: 尽管没人在听，他仍然说个不停。

examples.src: We must keep on working to reach our goal.
examples.dst: 我们必须继续努力以实现目标。

confuse.diff: keep on 是继续做；keep up 是保持（水平、速度）。

examples.src: She took a quick glance at her watch.
examples.dst: 她匆匆瞥了一眼手表。

examples.src: He glanced at the clock and hurried out of the room.
examples.dst: 他瞥了一眼时钟，匆忙走出房间。

examples.src: At first glance, the problem seemed easy.
examples.dst: 乍一看，这个问题似乎很简单。

confuse.diff: glance 是有意地瞥一眼；glimpse 是无意中瞥见。

examples.src: The economy has shown steady growth this year.
examples.dst: 今年经济呈现稳定增长。

examples.src: Hold the ladder steady while I climb up.
examples.dst: 我爬上去的时候请扶稳梯子。

examples.src: He took a deep breath to steady his nerves.
examples.dst: 他深吸一口气来稳定情绪。

confuse.diff: steady 是稳定的；study 是学习。

examples.src: The number of visitors has increased steadily.
examples.dst: 游客人数在持续增加。

examples.src: She worked steadily through the afternoon.
examples.dst: 她一下午都在稳步地工作。

examples.src: The rain fell steadily all night.
examples.dst: 雨整夜不停地下着。

confuse.diff: steadily 是稳步地；readily 是乐意地、轻易地。

examples.src: Teenagers have a tendency to stay up late.
examples.dst: 青少年有熬夜的倾向。

examples.src: There is a growing tendency to shop online.
examples.dst: 网上购物的趋势越来越明显。

examples.src: She has a tendency to worry too much about small things.
examples.dst: 她有为小事过分担忧的倾向。

confuse.diff: tendency 是倾向；intention 是意图。

examples.src: The disease was widespread in the area.
examples.dst: 这种疾病在该地区十分普遍。

examples.src: There is widespread concern about climate change.
examples.dst: 人们普遍关注气候变化。

examples.src: The use of smartphones has become widespread among students.
examples.dst: 智能手机在学生中已经普及。

confuse.diff: widespread 是形容词，意为广泛的；spread 是动词，意为传播。

examples.src: On the whole, the students did well in the exam.
examples.dst: 总的来说，学生们考得不错。

examples.src: On the whole, I agree with your opinion.
examples.dst: 大体上我同意你的看法。

examples.src: The trip was tiring, but on the whole it was enjoyable.
examples.dst: 旅途虽然累，但总体上还是愉快的。

confuse.diff: on the whole 是总的来说；as a whole 是作为整体。

examples.src: This small car is very economical to run.
examples.dst: 这辆小汽车开起来很省钱。

examples.src: It is more economical to buy in large quantities.
examples.dst: 大量购买更划算。

examples.src: She is economical with her pocket money.
examples.dst: 她花零用钱很节俭。

confuse.diff: economical 指节约的；economic 指经济（学）的。

examples.src: The farm covers an area of fifty hectares.
examples.dst: 这个农场占地五十公顷。

examples.src: Thousands of hectares of forest were destroyed by the fire.
examples.dst: 大火烧毁了数千公顷的森林。

examples.src: One hectare is equal to ten thousand square metres.
examples.dst: 一公顷等于一万平方米。

confuse.diff: hectare 是公顷；acre 是英亩，面积更小。

examples.src: The average age of the students is sixteen.
examples.dst: 这些学生的平均年龄是十六岁。

examples.src: On average, I sleep about seven hours a night.
examples.dst: 我平均每晚睡七个小时左右。

examples.src: His grades are above average in maths.
examples.dst: 他的数学成绩高于平均水平。

confuse.diff: average 强调平均水平；ordinary 强调普通、不特别。

examples.src: Scientists are searching for proof of life's existence on Mars.
examples.dst: 科学家们正在寻找火星上存在生命的证据。

examples.src: The company came into existence in 1998.
examples.dst: 这家公司成立于1998年。

examples.src: Pollution threatens the existence of many species.
examples.dst: 污染威胁着许多物种的生存。

confuse.diff: existence 是名词，存在；existent 是形容词，现存的。

examples.src: The outer layer of the fruit is quite hard.
examples.dst: 这种水果的外层相当硬。

examples.src: Scientists are exploring outer space with powerful telescopes.
examples.dst: 科学家们正用强大的望远镜探索外太空。

examples.src: He lives in an outer suburb of the city.
examples.dst: 他住在城市的远郊。

confuse.diff: outer 是形容词，只能放在名词前；outside 可作名词、副词、介词。

examples.src: I am speaking on behalf of all the students.
examples.dst: 我代表全体学生发言。

examples.src: She accepted the award on behalf of her team.
examples.dst: 她代表自己的团队领奖。

examples.src: The lawyer acted on behalf of his client.
examples.dst: 律师代表他的委托人行事。

confuse.diff: on behalf of 表示代表；in behalf of（美式）表示为了……的利益，较少用。

examples.src: Every individual has the right to education.
examples.dst: 每个人都有受教育的权利。

examples.src: The teacher gave individual attention to each student.
examples.dst: 老师对每个学生都给予个别关注。

examples.src: She has a very individual style of dressing.
examples.dst: 她的穿衣风格非常独特。

confuse.diff: individual 是名词或形容词；individually 是副词，单独地。

examples.src: Many experts advocate a healthy and balanced diet.
examples.dst: 许多专家提倡健康均衡的饮食。

examples.src: She is a strong advocate of equal education for girls.
examples.dst: 她是女孩平等受教育的坚定倡导者。

examples.src: The mayor advocated building more public parks.
examples.dst: 市长主张建造更多的公园。

confuse.diff: advocate 是倡导（者）；advocacy 是倡导、拥护这一行为。

examples.src: The company made a commitment to protect the environment.
examples.dst: 公司承诺保护环境。

examples.src: Success requires hard work and commitment.
examples.dst: 成功需要努力和投入。

examples.src: I can't join the club because of my other commitments.
examples.dst: 因为还有其他事务要忙，我无法加入这个俱乐部。

confuse.diff: commitment 是名词，承诺；commit 是动词，犯（罪）、承诺。

examples.src: I can't put up with the noise any longer.
examples.dst: 我再也无法忍受这种噪音了。

examples.src: She put up with the heat during the long journey.
examples.dst: 漫长的旅途中她忍受着酷热。

examples.src: We have to put up with some inconvenience during the repairs.
examples.dst: 维修期间我们得忍受一些不便。

confuse.diff: put up with 是忍受；put up 是张贴、搭建或留宿。

examples.src: Air pollution is a serious problem in big cities.
examples.dst: 空气污染是大城市的一个严重问题。

examples.src: The factory was fined for causing water pollution.
examples.dst: 这家工厂因造成水污染而被罚款。

examples.src: We should take action to reduce noise pollution.
examples.dst: 我们应该采取行动减少噪音污染。

confuse.diff: pollution 是污染；pollutant 是污染物质。

examples.src: The country has enjoyed rapid economic growth.
examples.dst: 这个国家经历了快速的经济增长。

examples.src: Good food is important for a child's growth.
examples.dst: 良好的饮食对孩子的成长很重要。

examples.src: There has been a growth in the number of online learners.
examples.dst: 在线学习者的数量有所增加。

confuse.diff: growth 是名词，增长；grow 是动词，生长。

examples.src: An electrical fault caused the fire.
examples.dst: 电路故障引起了这场火灾。

examples.src: He works as an electrical engineer in a power company.
examples.dst: 他在一家电力公司担任电气工程师。

examples.src: Switch off all electrical equipment before you leave.
examples.dst: 离开前请关掉所有电器设备。

confuse.diff: electrical 指与电有关的；electric 指用电的、带电的，如 electric car。

examples.src: A washing machine is a useful household appliance.
examples.dst: 洗衣机是一种有用的家用电器。

examples.src: Modern kitchens are full of electrical appliances.
examples.dst: 现代厨房里满是电器。

examples.src: Unplug the appliance before cleaning it.
examples.dst: 清洁电器前请先拔掉插头。

confuse.diff: appliance 是器具；application 是申请、应用。

examples.src: You can go out so long as you finish your homework.
examples.dst: 只要你完成作业，就可以出去。

examples.src: So long as you try your best, we will be proud of you.
examples.dst: 只要你尽力了，我们就会为你骄傲。

examples.src: I don't mind the weather so long as it doesn't rain.
examples.dst: 只要不下雨，我不在乎天气怎样。

confuse.diff: so long as 与 as long as 同义，前者更书面；as long as 还可表示时间长度。

examples.src: You can wear casual clothes to the party.
examples.dst: 你可以穿便装去参加聚会。

examples.src: They had a casual chat in the corridor.
examples.dst: 他们在走廊里随意聊了几句。

examples.src: It was just a casual remark, so don't take it seriously.
examples.dst: 那只是随口一说，别当真。

confuse.diff: casual 是随意的；causal 是因果的。

examples.src: We study maths, physics, chemistry and so on.
examples.dst: 我们学习数学、物理、化学等等。

examples.src: She likes reading, painting, swimming and so on.
examples.dst: 她喜欢阅读、绘画、游泳等等。

examples.src: The shop sells pens, notebooks, rulers and so on.
examples.dst: 这家店出售钢笔、笔记本、尺子等等。

confuse.diff: 两者意思相近，and so forth 稍显正式。

examples.src: The motor of the boat suddenly stopped working.
examples.dst: 小船的发动机突然停止了运转。

examples.src: This toy car is driven by a small electric motor.
examples.dst: 这个玩具车由一个小电动机驱动。

examples.src: The motor industry provides jobs for millions of people.
examples.dst: 汽车工业为数百万人提供了就业机会。

confuse.diff: motor 多指电动机；engine 多指燃料发动机。

examples.src: He opened a can of tomato soup for lunch.
examples.dst: 他打开一罐番茄汤当午饭。

examples.src: The factory cans fruit and sells it abroad.
examples.dst: 这家工厂把水果装罐后销往国外。

examples.src: Can you help me with this problem?
examples.dst: 你能帮我解决这个问题吗？

confuse.diff: can 是现在的能力；could 是过去的能力或更委婉的语气。

examples.src: Under no circumstances should you open this door.
examples.dst: 无论如何你都不应该打开这扇门。

examples.src: He succeeded in difficult circumstances.
examples.dst: 他在困难的环境中取得了成功。

examples.src: The match was cancelled due to circumstances beyond our control.
examples.dst: 由于不可控的情况，比赛被取消了。

confuse.diff: circumstance 是情况；circumference 是圆周。

examples.src: I heated my lunch in the microwave.
examples.dst: 我用微波炉加热了午饭。

examples.src: Microwave the soup for two minutes.
examples.dst: 把汤放进微波炉加热两分钟。

examples.src: Microwaves are widely used in communication.
examples.dst: 微波被广泛应用于通信领域。

confuse.diff: microwave 用微波加热；oven 是烤箱，用热空气烘烤。

examples.src: A cold shower will refresh you after the long trip.
examples.dst: 长途旅行后冲个冷水澡会让你恢复精神。

examples.src: Try to refresh the page if it does not load.
examples.dst: 如果页面加载不出来，试着刷新一下。

examples.src: Let me refresh your memory about what happened last week.
examples.dst: 让我帮你回忆一下上周发生的事。

confuse.diff: refresh 是使恢复精神；refrain 是克制、避免。

examples.src: She has worked as an educator for over twenty years.
examples.dst: 她从事教育工作已有二十多年。

examples.src: Educators are discussing how to reduce students' homework.
examples.dst: 教育工作者们正在讨论如何减轻学生的作业负担。

examples.src: Confucius is regarded as a great educator in China.
examples.dst: 孔子被视为中国伟大的教育家。

confuse.diff: educator 是教育者；education 是教育。

examples.src: He made a great contribution to the development of science.
examples.dst: 他对科学的发展做出了巨大贡献。

examples.src: Every contribution to the fund is welcome.
examples.dst: 欢迎为基金会提供任何捐助。

examples.src: Her contribution to the school newspaper was well received.
examples.dst: 她给校报的投稿很受欢迎。

confuse.diff: contribution 是贡献；distribution 是分发、分布。

examples.src: It is imperative that we act now to protect the forests.
examples.dst: 我们必须立即行动来保护森林。

examples.src: Speed is imperative in an emergency.
examples.dst: 紧急情况下速度至关重要。

examples.src: Open the door is an imperative sentence.
examples.dst: Open the door 是一个祈使句。

confuse.diff: imperative 是必要的；imperfect 是不完美的。

examples.src: Write a heading at the top of each paragraph.
examples.dst: 在每一段的上方写一个小标题。

examples.src: The heading of the article caught my attention.
examples.dst: 这篇文章的标题引起了我的注意。

examples.src: Choose the best heading for the passage.
examples.dst: 为这篇短文选择最合适的标题。

confuse.diff: heading 是章节小标题；headline 是报纸的大标题。

examples.src: The company's slogan is easy to remember.
examples.dst: 这家公司的广告语很好记。

examples.src: Students shouted slogans during the sports meeting.
examples.dst: 运动会上学生们高喊口号。

examples.src: We need a catchy slogan for our environmental campaign.
examples.dst: 我们的环保活动需要一个朗朗上口的口号。

confuse.diff: slogan 多用于广告或宣传；motto 指座右铭。

examples.src: She gave a presentation about her research project.
examples.dst: 她就自己的研究项目做了一次展示。

examples.src: The presentation of the prizes will begin at noon.
examples.dst: 颁奖仪式将在中午开始。

examples.src: Good presentation skills will help you in your career.
examples.dst: 良好的演讲展示技巧会对你的职业生涯有帮助。

confuse.diff: presentation 是演示、展示；present 可作礼物、目前的或赠送。

examples.src: The country plans to build a new nuclear power station.
examples.dst: 该国计划建一座新的核电站。

examples.src: Nuclear energy can produce a great deal of electricity.
examples.dst: 核能可以产生大量电力。

examples.src: Many people hope the world will be free of nuclear weapons.
examples.dst: 许多人希望世界上没有核武器。

confuse.diff: nuclear 是形容词，核的；nucleus 是名词，原子核或核心。

examples.src: They had a disagreement about how to spend the money.
examples.dst: 他们在如何花这笔钱上有分歧。

examples.src: There is still disagreement among scientists on this issue.
examples.dst: 科学家们在这个问题上仍有分歧。

examples.src: A small disagreement should not destroy a friendship.
examples.dst: 一点小分歧不应毁掉友谊。

confuse.diff: disagreement 是名词，分歧；disagree 是动词，不同意。

examples.src: The teacher drew a diagram on the blackboard.
examples.dst: 老师在黑板上画了一张示意图。

examples.src: Look at the diagram and explain how the machine works.
examples.dst: 看着这张图，解释一下这台机器是如何工作的。

examples.src: The diagram shows the water cycle in nature.
examples.dst: 这张图展示了自然界中的水循环。

confuse.diff: diagram 是图表；program 是程序、节目。

examples.src: The volcano has been quiet for hundreds of years.
examples.dst: 这座火山已沉寂了数百年。

examples.src: Mount Fuji is a famous volcano in Japan.
examples.dst: 富士山是日本著名的火山。

examples.src: The volcano erupted without any warning.
examples.dst: 火山毫无预兆地喷发了。

confuse.diff: volcano 是名词，火山；volcanic 是形容词，火山的。

examples.src: Volcanic ash covered the whole town.
examples.dst: 火山灰覆盖了整个小镇。

examples.src: The island was formed by volcanic activity.
examples.dst: 这座岛屿是由火山活动形成的。

examples.src: Volcanic soil is rich and good for farming.
examples.dst: 火山土壤肥沃，适合耕种。

confuse.diff: volcanic 是形容词，火山的；volcano 是名词，火山。

examples.src: She is studying volcanology at university.
examples.dst: 她正在大学里学习火山学。

examples.src: Volcanology helps us predict dangerous eruptions.
examples.dst: 火山学帮助我们预测危险的火山喷发。

examples.src: He wrote a book on the history of volcanology.
examples.dst: 他写了一本关于火山学历史的书。

confuse.diff: volcanology 是学科；volcanologist 是火山学家。

examples.src: The volcanologist climbed up to collect rock samples.
examples.dst: 火山学家爬上山去采集岩石样本。

examples.src: Volcanologists watch the mountain day and night.
examples.dst: 火山学家日夜监测这座山。

examples.src: A volcanologist warned the villagers to leave at once.
examples.dst: 一位火山学家警告村民立即撤离。

confuse.diff: volcanologist 是火山学家；volcanology 是火山学。

examples.src: The volcano erupted and sent ash high into the sky.
examples.dst: 火山喷发，把火山灰喷向高空。

examples.src: Fighting erupted in the streets after the match.
examples.dst: 比赛结束后街上爆发了冲突。

examples.src: The crowd erupted into cheers when the team scored.
examples.dst: 球队得分时，人群爆发出欢呼声。

confuse.diff: erupt 是喷发、爆发；interrupt 是打断。

examples.src: The eruption forced thousands of people to leave their homes.
examples.dst: 火山喷发迫使数千人离开家园。

examples.src: Scientists tried to predict the time of the next eruption.
examples.dst: 科学家们试图预测下一次喷发的时间。

examples.src: The sudden eruption of anger surprised everyone.
examples.dst: 突然爆发的怒火让所有人吃了一惊。

confuse.diff: eruption 是喷发；interruption 是打断。

examples.src: The fire left nothing but ash behind.
examples.dst: 大火过后只剩下灰烬。

examples.src: Volcanic ash made it hard to breathe.
examples.dst: 火山灰使人呼吸困难。

examples.src: Be careful not to drop cigarette ash on the carpet.
examples.dst: 小心别把烟灰掉在地毯上。

confuse.diff: ash 是灰；ask 是询问。

examples.src: Smoke was rising from the crater of the volcano.
examples.dst: 火山口正冒着浓烟。

examples.src: The surface of the moon is covered with craters.
examples.dst: 月球表面布满了陨石坑。

examples.src: The tourists walked to the edge of the crater.
examples.dst: 游客们走到了火山口的边缘。

confuse.diff: crater 是火山口；creator 是创造者。

examples.src: Hot lava flowed down the side of the mountain.
examples.dst: 炽热的熔岩顺着山坡流下。

examples.src: The lava destroyed several houses near the volcano.
examples.dst: 熔岩摧毁了火山附近的几座房屋。

examples.src: When lava cools, it becomes hard rock.
examples.dst: 熔岩冷却后会变成坚硬的岩石。

confuse.diff: lava 是熔岩；larva 是幼虫。

examples.src: The hurricane destroyed hundreds of homes along the coast.
examples.dst: 飓风摧毁了沿海数百座房屋。

examples.src: Residents were told to leave before the hurricane arrived.
examples.dst: 居民被告知在飓风到来之前撤离。

examples.src: Hurricanes usually form over warm ocean water.
examples.dst: 飓风通常在温暖的海面上形成。

confuse.diff: hurricane 指大西洋和东太平洋的风暴；typhoon 指西太平洋的台风。

examples.src: Students were asked to fill in a questionnaire about their study habits.
examples.dst: 学生们被要求填写一份关于学习习惯的问卷。

examples.src: The results of the questionnaire surprised the teachers.
examples.dst: 问卷调查的结果让老师们很惊讶。

examples.src: We designed a questionnaire to find out what people think.
examples.dst: 我们设计了一份问卷来了解人们的想法。

confuse.diff: questionnaire 是整份问卷；question 是单个问题。

examples.src: The boat pulled up alongside the pier.
examples.dst: 小船靠到了码头边。

examples.src: She worked alongside experts from many countries.
examples.dst: 她与来自许多国家的专家一起工作。

examples.src: Traditional methods are used alongside modern technology.
examples.dst: 传统方法与现代技术并用。

confuse.diff: alongside 强调并排；along 表示沿着。

examples.src: The laboratory is full of expensive equipment.
examples.dst: 实验室里满是昂贵的设备。

examples.src: We need some new sports equipment for the school team.
examples.dst: 我们需要为校队添置一些新的运动器材。

examples.src: This equipment is used to measure air quality.
examples.dst: 这台设备用来测量空气质量。

confuse.diff: equipment 是不可数名词，设备；equip 是动词，装备。

examples.src: The school appointed her as the new head teacher.
examples.dst: 学校任命她为新校长。

examples.src: They appointed a date for the meeting.
examples.dst: 他们约定了会议的日期。

examples.src: He was appointed captain of the football team.
examples.dst: 他被任命为足球队队长。

confuse.diff: appoint 是任命；disappoint 是使失望。

examples.src: The class visited an observatory to look at the stars.
examples.dst: 全班参观了一个天文台去观察星星。

examples.src: The volcano observatory records every small earthquake.
examples.dst: 火山观测站记录每一次小地震。

examples.src: The observatory stands on top of a high mountain.
examples.dst: 天文台坐落在一座高山的山顶上。

confuse.diff: observatory 是观测站；observation 是观察。

examples.src: The library keeps all its records in a database.
examples.dst: 图书馆把所有记录都保存在数据库中。

examples.src: Scientists built a database of volcanic eruptions.
examples.dst: 科学家们建立了一个火山喷发数据库。

examples.src: You can search the database by name or number.
examples.dst: 你可以按姓名或编号搜索数据库。

confuse.diff: database 是数据库；data 是数据本身。

examples.src: Teachers evaluate students' progress every term.
examples.dst: 老师每学期评估学生的进步情况。

examples.src: We need to evaluate the risks before making a decision.
examples.dst: 做决定之前，我们需要评估风险。

examples.src: It is difficult to evaluate the effect of the new policy.
examples.dst: 很难评估这项新政策的效果。

confuse.diff: evaluate 是评估；evaporate 是蒸发。

examples.src: The old wooden house burned to the ground last night.
examples.dst: 那座旧木屋昨晚被烧成了平地。

examples.src: The fire burned the whole village to the ground.
examples.dst: 大火把整个村庄烧成了废墟。

examples.src: The factory was burned to the ground in a few hours.
examples.dst: 这家工厂在几个小时内被烧毁殆尽。

confuse.diff: burn to the ground 强调被烧得一干二净；burn down 指烧毁。

examples.src: A huge wave hit the rocks along the shore.
examples.dst: 一个巨浪拍打着海岸的岩石。

examples.src: She waved goodbye to her friends at the station.
examples.dst: 她在车站向朋友们挥手告别。

examples.src: A wave of excitement ran through the crowd.
examples.dst: 一阵兴奋的情绪传遍了人群。

confuse.diff: wave 是波浪、挥手；waive 是放弃（权利）。

examples.src: Molten rock flowed out of the volcano.
examples.dst: 熔融的岩石从火山中流出。

examples.src: The workers poured molten iron into the mould.
examples.dst: 工人们把铁水倒进模具中。

examples.src: Deep under the ground, the rock is hot and molten.
examples.dst: 在地下深处，岩石炽热并呈熔融状态。

confuse.diff: molten 是熔化的；mountain 是山。

examples.src: Children were playing around the fountain in the square.
examples.dst: 孩子们在广场的喷泉旁玩耍。

examples.src: A fountain of lava shot into the air.
examples.dst: 一股熔岩喷泉冲向空中。

examples.src: She is a fountain of knowledge on local history.
examples.dst: 她是本地历史知识的源泉。

confuse.diff: fountain 是喷泉；mountain 是山，两词拼写相近。

examples.src: I have absolute trust in my teammates.
examples.dst: 我完全信任我的队友。

examples.src: The room was in absolute silence.
examples.dst: 房间里一片寂静。

examples.src: There is no absolute standard of beauty.
examples.dst: 美没有绝对的标准。

confuse.diff: absolute 是绝对的；absorb 是吸收。

examples.src: You are absolutely right about this problem.
examples.dst: 关于这个问题你说得完全正确。

examples.src: It is absolutely necessary to wear a helmet here.
examples.dst: 在这里戴头盔是绝对必要的。

examples.src: Do you agree with me? Absolutely!
examples.dst: 你同意我的看法吗？当然！

confuse.diff: absolutely 是副词；absolute 是形容词。

examples.src: The little boy dreams of becoming a spaceman.
examples.dst: 这个小男孩梦想成为一名宇航员。

examples.src: The spaceman waved to the camera before the launch.
examples.dst: 发射前，宇航员向镜头挥了挥手。

examples.src: Spacemen must train for years before they fly.
examples.dst: 宇航员在飞行之前必须训练多年。

confuse.diff: spaceman 较口语；astronaut 是正式用词。

examples.src: He wore a dark suit to the interview.
examples.dst: 他穿着深色西装去面试。

examples.src: Astronauts wear special suits in space.
examples.dst: 宇航员在太空中穿着特制的服装。

examples.src: This job suits you well.
examples.dst: 这份工作很适合你。

confuse.diff: suit 是套装或适合；suite 是套房，发音不同。

examples.src: You must wear a helmet when riding a bike.
examples.dst: 骑自行车时你必须戴头盔。

examples.src: The workers put on their helmets before entering the site.
examples.dst: 工人们进入工地前戴上了安全帽。

examples.src: The helmet saved his life in the accident.
examples.dst: 头盔在事故中救了他的命。

confuse.diff: helmet 是头盔；helmsman 是舵手。

examples.src: She bought a pair of warm boots for winter.
examples.dst: 她为冬天买了一双保暖的靴子。

examples.src: He put the bags in the boot of the car.
examples.dst: 他把包放进了汽车后备厢。

examples.src: It takes a minute for the computer to boot up.
examples.dst: 电脑启动需要一分钟。

confuse.diff: boot 是靴子；boost 是促进、提升。

examples.src: The climbers made their way slowly up the mountain.
examples.dst: 登山者们缓缓向山上前进。

examples.src: She made her way through the crowd to the stage.
examples.dst: 她穿过人群走向舞台。

examples.src: He made his way in the world through hard work.
examples.dst: 他靠努力在社会上闯出了一片天地。

confuse.diff: make one’s way 是前往；make way 是让路。

examples.src: The boy has great potential as a musician.
examples.dst: 这个男孩作为音乐家很有潜力。

examples.src: We must think about the potential dangers of the plan.
examples.dst: 我们必须考虑这个计划潜在的危险。

examples.src: The school helps students develop their full potential.
examples.dst: 学校帮助学生充分发挥他们的潜能。

confuse.diff: potential 是潜在的；potent 是强有力的。

examples.src: The actual cost was higher than we expected.
examples.dst: 实际费用比我们预想的要高。

examples.src: What were his actual words?
examples.dst: 他的原话是什么？

examples.src: The film is based on an actual event.
examples.dst: 这部电影根据真实事件改编。

confuse.diff: actual 是实际的；current 是当前的。

examples.src: She is interested in geology and often collects rocks.
examples.dst: 她对地质学感兴趣，常常收集岩石。

examples.src: Geology can tell us how mountains were formed.
examples.dst: 地质学能告诉我们山脉是如何形成的。

examples.src: He is a professor of geology at a famous university.
examples.dst: 他是一所著名大学的地质学教授。

confuse.diff: geology 是地质学；geography 是地理学。

examples.src: The scientists collected samples of rock from the moon.
examples.dst: 科学家们从月球上采集了岩石样本。

examples.src: You can get a free sample of the new shampoo.
examples.dst: 你可以领取这款新洗发水的免费试用装。

examples.src: We sampled some local dishes during the trip.
examples.dst: 旅行期间我们品尝了一些当地菜肴。

confuse.diff: sample 是样品；simple 是简单的。

examples.src: Each candidate will have five minutes to speak.
examples.dst: 每位候选人有五分钟的发言时间。

examples.src: Several candidates are applying for the job.
examples.dst: 好几位求职者在申请这份工作。

examples.src: The candidates are waiting outside the examination hall.
examples.dst: 考生们正在考场外等候。

confuse.diff: candidate 是候选人；candy 是糖果。

examples.src: Pollution is a serious threat to public health.
examples.dst: 污染对公众健康构成严重威胁。

examples.src: He received a threat from an unknown person.
examples.dst: 他收到了一个陌生人的威胁。

examples.src: The dark clouds were a threat of heavy rain.
examples.dst: 乌云预示着大雨将至。

confuse.diff: threat 是威胁；treat 是对待、款待。

examples.src: My grandparents live in a small bungalow by the sea.
examples.dst: 我的祖父母住在海边的一座小平房里。

examples.src: The bungalow has a garden full of flowers.
examples.dst: 这座平房有一个种满鲜花的花园。

examples.src: They bought a bungalow in the countryside.
examples.dst: 他们在乡下买了一座平房。

confuse.diff: bungalow 是单层住宅；cottage 是乡间小屋，可以有两层。

examples.src: A tornado swept through the town and destroyed many houses.
examples.dst: 一场龙卷风席卷小镇，摧毁了许多房屋。

examples.src: The family hid in the basement during the tornado.
examples.dst: 龙卷风来袭时，这家人躲进了地下室。

examples.src: Tornadoes often happen in the central United States.
examples.dst: 龙卷风常发生在美国中部。

confuse.diff: tornado 是陆地上的龙卷风；typhoon 是海上形成的台风。

examples.src: The typhoon hit the coast of Guangdong last night.
examples.dst: 台风昨晚袭击了广东沿海。

examples.src: All flights were cancelled because of the typhoon.
examples.dst: 由于台风，所有航班都被取消了。

examples.src: Fishermen returned to the port before the typhoon came.
examples.dst: 台风来临前，渔民们回到了港口。

confuse.diff: typhoon 指西北太平洋的台风；hurricane 指大西洋的飓风。

examples.src: A violent thunderstorm broke out in the afternoon.
examples.dst: 下午爆发了一场猛烈的雷暴。

examples.src: We stayed inside during the thunderstorm.
examples.dst: 雷雨期间我们待在室内。

examples.src: The thunderstorm knocked out the power in the whole area.
examples.dst: 雷暴使整个地区停电。

confuse.diff: thunderstorm 是雷暴；thunder 只指雷声。

examples.src: Time is precious, so don't waste it.
examples.dst: 时间宝贵，不要浪费。

examples.src: The museum keeps many precious stones.
examples.dst: 博物馆里收藏着许多珍贵的宝石。

examples.src: The photo is precious to her because it shows her grandmother.
examples.dst: 这张照片对她来说很珍贵，因为上面有她的祖母。

confuse.diff: precious 是珍贵的；previous 是先前的。

examples.src: Lu Xun was a great novelist and thinker.
examples.dst: 鲁迅是一位伟大的小说家和思想家。

examples.src: The young novelist is writing her first book.
examples.dst: 这位年轻的小说家正在写她的第一本书。

examples.src: Many novelists get their ideas from daily life.
examples.dst: 许多小说家从日常生活中获得灵感。

confuse.diff: novelist 是小说家；novel 是小说。

examples.src: Thick fog made driving very dangerous this morning.
examples.dst: 今天早上浓雾让开车变得很危险。

examples.src: The airport was closed because of the fog.
examples.dst: 机场因大雾而关闭。

examples.src: The mountains disappeared in the fog.
examples.dst: 群山消失在雾中。

confuse.diff: fog 是雾；frog 是青蛙。

examples.src: Please bring all the necessary documents to the interview.
examples.dst: 请把所有必要的文件带到面试现场。

examples.src: She saved the document on her computer.
examples.dst: 她把文档保存在了电脑里。

examples.src: The journalist documented the damage caused by the flood.
examples.dst: 记者记录了洪水造成的损失。

confuse.diff: document 是文件；documentary 是纪录片。

examples.src: A beautiful rainbow appeared after the rain.
examples.dst: 雨后出现了一道美丽的彩虹。

examples.src: A rainbow has seven colours.
examples.dst: 彩虹有七种颜色。

examples.src: The children pointed at the rainbow in the sky.
examples.dst: 孩子们指着天上的彩虹。

examples.src: This chair is hard and uncomfortable.
examples.dst: 这把椅子又硬又不舒服。

examples.src: I felt uncomfortable when everyone looked at me.
examples.dst: 大家都看着我时，我感到不自在。

examples.src: There was an uncomfortable silence in the room.
examples.dst: 房间里出现了令人尴尬的沉默。

confuse.diff: uncomfortable 是不舒服的；comfortable 是舒服的。

examples.src: We had breakfast on the balcony in the sun.
examples.dst: 我们在阳台上晒着太阳吃早餐。

examples.src: She grows flowers on her balcony.
examples.dst: 她在阳台上种花。

examples.src: We had seats in the balcony of the theatre.
examples.dst: 我们在剧院的楼座有座位。

confuse.diff: balcony 是从楼房墙壁伸出的阳台；terrace 常指平台或梯田。

examples.src: The driver was unconscious when the ambulance arrived.
examples.dst: 救护车到达时，司机已失去知觉。

examples.src: She was unconscious of the danger around her.
examples.dst: 她没有意识到周围的危险。

examples.src: Biting nails can be an unconscious habit.
examples.dst: 咬指甲可能是一种无意识的习惯。

confuse.diff: unconscious 指失去知觉或未察觉；subconscious 指潜意识的。

examples.src: The hunter raised his gun and shot at the bird.
examples.dst: 猎人举起枪朝鸟射击。

examples.src: The film was shot in a small village in Yunnan.
examples.dst: 这部电影是在云南的一个小村庄拍摄的。

examples.src: He shot the ball into the net in the last minute.
examples.dst: 他在最后一分钟把球射进了网里。

confuse.diff: shoot 是射击；shout 是大喊。

examples.src: We heard a shot in the distance.
examples.dst: 我们听到远处传来一声枪响。

examples.src: The photographer took a beautiful shot of the sunrise.
examples.dst: 摄影师拍了一张美丽的日出照片。

examples.src: The nurse gave him a flu shot.
examples.dst: 护士给他打了一针流感疫苗。

confuse.diff: shot 是射击、镜头；short 是短的。

examples.src: Her hands trembled with fear.
examples.dst: 她的双手因恐惧而发抖。

examples.src: The ground trembled during the earthquake.
examples.dst: 地震时大地在颤抖。

examples.src: His voice trembled as he began to speak.
examples.dst: 他开始说话时声音在颤抖。

confuse.diff: tremble 是发抖；resemble 是像、类似。

examples.src: Sweat ran down his face after the long race.
examples.dst: 长跑之后，汗水顺着他的脸流下来。

examples.src: You will sweat a lot if you exercise in this heat.
examples.dst: 在这样的高温下运动你会出很多汗。

examples.src: He was sweating with nervousness before the exam.
examples.dst: 考试前他紧张得直冒汗。

confuse.diff: sweat 是汗水；sweater 是毛衣。

examples.src: Her parents were anxious about her safety.
examples.dst: 她的父母很担心她的安全。

examples.src: The students were anxious to know their exam results.
examples.dst: 学生们急于知道考试成绩。

examples.src: He felt anxious before the interview.
examples.dst: 面试前他感到焦虑。

confuse.diff: anxious 是形容词，焦虑的；anxiety 是名词，焦虑。

examples.src: Many students feel anxiety before important exams.
examples.dst: 许多学生在重要考试前感到焦虑。

examples.src: She waited for the news with great anxiety.
examples.dst: 她焦急万分地等待着消息。

examples.src: Regular exercise can help reduce stress and anxiety.
examples.dst: 经常锻炼有助于缓解压力和焦虑。

confuse.diff: anxiety 是名词，焦虑；anxious 是形容词，焦虑的。

examples.src: Panic broke out when the fire alarm rang.
examples.dst: 火警响起时，人群陷入恐慌。

examples.src: Don't panic. Everything will be fine.
examples.dst: 别慌，一切都会好的。

examples.src: The news caused panic among the villagers.
examples.dst: 这个消息在村民中引起了恐慌。

confuse.diff: panic 是恐慌；picnic 是野餐。

examples.src: The earthquake under the sea caused a huge tsunami.
examples.dst: 海底地震引发了一场巨大的海啸。

examples.src: The tsunami destroyed many towns along the coast.
examples.dst: 海啸摧毁了沿海的许多城镇。

examples.src: A warning system can give people time to escape a tsunami.
examples.dst: 预警系统能给人们留出逃离海啸的时间。

confuse.diff: tsunami 是海啸，由海底地震引起；typhoon 是台风，由气旋引起。

examples.src: I glanced through the newspaper while having breakfast.
examples.dst: 我吃早饭时浏览了一下报纸。

examples.src: She glanced through the report before the meeting.
examples.dst: 开会前她快速浏览了一遍报告。

examples.src: Please glance through the questions before you start writing.
examples.dst: 开始写之前，请先浏览一遍题目。

confuse.diff: glance through 是浏览整篇内容；glance at 是瞥一眼。

examples.src: The Manchu people founded the Qing Dynasty.
examples.dst: 满族人建立了清朝。

examples.src: She is a Manchu and speaks some Manchu words.
examples.dst: 她是满族人，会说一些满语词汇。

examples.src: The museum shows traditional Manchu clothing.
examples.dst: 博物馆展出了传统的满族服饰。

confuse.diff: Manchu 指满族；Mandarin 指普通话。

examples.src: Prices vary from ten yuan to a hundred yuan.
examples.dst: 价格从十元到一百元不等。

examples.src: The temperature varies from day to day in spring.
examples.dst: 春天的气温每天都不一样。

examples.src: Students' interests vary from sports to music.
examples.dst: 学生们的兴趣涵盖从体育到音乐。

confuse.diff: vary from…to… 表示变化范围；vary in 表示在某方面不同。

examples.src: China is a country with diverse cultures.
examples.dst: 中国是一个文化多样的国家。

examples.src: The school offers a diverse range of activities.
examples.dst: 学校提供种类繁多的活动。

examples.src: The class is made up of students from diverse backgrounds.
examples.dst: 这个班级由不同背景的学生组成。

confuse.diff: diverse 是多样的；diverge 是分叉、偏离。

examples.src: The rainforest is famous for its biological diversity.
examples.dst: 热带雨林以其生物多样性而闻名。

examples.src: We should respect the diversity of cultures.
examples.dst: 我们应该尊重文化的多样性。

examples.src: There is great diversity in the opinions of the students.
examples.dst: 学生们的意见存在很大的差异。

confuse.diff: diversity 是多样性；university 是大学。

examples.src: A red-crowned crane stood quietly in the lake.
examples.dst: 一只丹顶鹤静静地立在湖中。

examples.src: A huge crane was lifting steel beams at the building site.
examples.dst: 一台巨大的起重机正在工地上吊钢梁。

examples.src: In China, the crane is a symbol of long life.
examples.dst: 在中国，鹤是长寿的象征。

confuse.diff: crane 是鹤或起重机；crate 是板条箱。

examples.src: A leopard is waiting quietly in the tree.
examples.dst: 一只豹子正静静地在树上等待。

examples.src: Leopards can run very fast and climb trees.
examples.dst: 豹子跑得很快，还会爬树。

examples.src: The snow leopard is an endangered animal.
examples.dst: 雪豹是一种濒危动物。

confuse.diff: leopard 是豹，身上有环状斑点；cheetah 是猎豹，跑得最快。

means: 壮观的；引人注目的；惊人的

examples.src: We enjoyed the spectacular view from the top of the mountain.
examples.dst: 我们欣赏了山顶上壮观的景色。

examples.src: The team won a spectacular victory in the final.
examples.dst: 球队在决赛中取得了辉煌的胜利。

examples.src: The fireworks display was absolutely spectacular.
examples.dst: 烟花表演真是壮观极了。

confuse.diff: spectacular 是壮观的；spectacle 是景象、奇观。

examples.src: The baby is bathed every evening before bed.
examples.dst: 婴儿每天晚上睡前都要洗澡。

examples.src: The hills were bathed in golden sunlight.
examples.dst: 山丘沐浴在金色的阳光中。

examples.src: Tourists like to bathe in the warm sea.
examples.dst: 游客们喜欢在温暖的海水里游泳。

confuse.diff: bathe 是动词，发音带 /ð/；bath 是名词，洗澡、浴缸。

examples.src: The strange noise aroused my curiosity.
examples.dst: 奇怪的声音引起了我的好奇心。

examples.src: The speech aroused people's interest in protecting wildlife.
examples.dst: 这次演讲唤起了人们保护野生动物的兴趣。

examples.src: She was aroused from sleep by a loud knock at the door.
examples.dst: 一阵响亮的敲门声把她从睡梦中惊醒。

confuse.diff: arouse 是唤起；arise 是出现、产生。

examples.src: She sent a card to show her appreciation for our help.
examples.dst: 她寄了一张卡片对我们的帮助表示感谢。

examples.src: The course aims to develop students' appreciation of music.
examples.dst: 这门课程旨在培养学生的音乐鉴赏力。

examples.src: He has little appreciation of how hard his parents work.
examples.dst: 他不太理解父母工作有多辛苦。

confuse.diff: appreciation 是名词；appreciate 是动词，感激、欣赏。

examples.src: The climbers reached the peak at dawn.
examples.dst: 登山者在黎明时分到达了山顶。

examples.src: Traffic is at its peak between seven and nine in the morning.
examples.dst: 早上七点到九点是交通高峰。

examples.src: Her career peaked when she was thirty.
examples.dst: 她的事业在三十岁时达到顶峰。

confuse.diff: peak 是山顶；pick 是挑选、采摘。

examples.src: After much persuasion, he agreed to join the club.
examples.dst: 经过再三劝说，他同意加入俱乐部。

examples.src: She has great powers of persuasion.
examples.dst: 她有很强的说服力。

examples.src: It took a lot of persuasion to make him change his mind.
examples.dst: 花了很多功夫劝说才让他改变主意。

confuse.diff: persuasion 是名词，说服；persuade 是动词，说服。

examples.src: This watch comes with a two-year guarantee.
examples.dst: 这块手表有两年保修。

examples.src: I can't guarantee that it will not rain tomorrow.
examples.dst: 我不能保证明天不下雨。

examples.src: Hard work is no guarantee of success, but it helps.
examples.dst: 努力不能保证成功，但很有帮助。

confuse.diff: guarantee 是保证；guard 是守卫、保卫。
